title: Your bad habits run on autopilot

scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: Why do bad habits feel automatic?
scenes.voiceover: Why do bad habits feel automatic?

scenes.visual: Triangle habit loop: CUE (mustard) → ROUTINE (coral) → REWARD (teal) nodes with arrows; a navy dot travels the loop and the active node swells.
scenes.voiceover: Every habit is a loop. A cue triggers a routine, and the routine pays off in a reward.

scenes.visual: A navy steering wheel turns by itself while mustard Zzz bubbles float up — the brain has handed over control.
scenes.voiceover: Repeat it enough and your brain hands the wheel to autopilot. The cue fires and you're moving before you decide.

scenes.visual: The same loop; the middle ROUTINE node (old, coral) slides out and a new teal routine springs in from above, while CUE and REWARD stay put.
scenes.voiceover: So don't fight the cue. Keep it — and the reward — but swap the routine in the middle.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it the habit loop runs as one automatic cycle — the basal ganglia chunking the whole thing.
scenes.cardText: Habits get 'chunked' in the basal ganglia — one automatic unit.
scenes.voiceover: Deep in the brain, the basal ganglia chunk the whole loop into one automatic unit, so it runs without effort.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the routine-swap animation plays with the new teal routine dropping in. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
Keep the cue, swap the routine.
Same trigger, better payoff.
scenes.voiceover: Pick one bad habit. Keep its cue, but swap in a routine you actually want.
